name: AF Rotor Research Topics — Quality Rubric

questions.question: Are there exactly 5 distinct, non-overlapping topic titles (not fewer, not more)?
questions.evaluationGuidance: Fail if fewer or more than 5, or if any two topics substantially overlap.

questions.question: Does each topic include a one-sentence rationale grounded in plausible pathophysiology?
questions.evaluationGuidance: Every topic must link its proposed idea to a mechanism. Missing rationale on any topic fails.

questions.question: Do the topics span at least 3 distinct mechanistic domains (e.g., ion-channel/electrophysiology, fibrosis/structural substrate, mapping methodology, autonomic modulation)?
questions.evaluationGuidance: Score 3+ passes. Count unique mechanistic domains represented across the 5 topics.

questions.question: Does the answer clearly distinguish hypothesis-generating ideas from established evidence?
questions.evaluationGuidance: Conflating guideline recommendations with mechanistic evidence fails this question.

questions.question: Does the answer use precise scientific language and avoid vague or generic AF topic phrasing?
questions.evaluationGuidance: Generic AF topics without specific rotor-mechanism focus fail.

questions.question: Are the topics grounded in or cross-checked against the cardiology-canon-v2 bookshelf, with source citations where evidence is claimed?
questions.evaluationGuidance: Claims of established evidence should cite indexed sources; ungrounded evidence claims fail.
